exam-1-s1.title: Visitors to a pop-up museum
exam-1-s1.html:
A pop-up museum counted its visitors each week. Use a graphing calculator, and store each regression with all its digits.

Number of visitors V during week x after a pop-up museum opened
xx (week)1234567
VV (visitors)42617380787155

items.q: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -0.5x^3 + 3x^2 - 2x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the relative maximum value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> on the interval <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < x < 6</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.355</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.355</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.633</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.633</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.645</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.645</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> in a window such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 6</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-12 \le y \le 12</annotation></semantics></math> and use the calculator's maximum feature. The high point between the two turning points is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.633</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 3.633</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>9.355</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x) \approx 9.355</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluate <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> at the stored <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-value rather than at a rounded one.
options: Right: the greatest output near the turning point at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.633</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 3.633</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> changes from increasing to decreasing.

This is the input where the relative maximum occurs; the question asks for the value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> there.

This is the relative minimum value, at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.367</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 0.367</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> changes from decreasing to increasing.

This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(0)</annotation></semantics></math>, the value at the left end of the interval, which is lower than the high point.

items.q: Use a graphing calculator to find every real zero of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.700</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.700</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.239</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.239</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.461</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.461</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.239</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.239</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.461</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.461</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3.461</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3.461</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.239</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.239</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.700</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.700</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.131</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.131</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.535</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.535</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: A cubic has at most three real zeros. Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> in a window that shows both turning points and both ends, such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2 \le x \le 5</annotation></semantics></math>, and use the zero feature for each <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-intercept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.700</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -0.700</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.239</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.239</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.461</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 3.461</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: all three <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-intercepts of the graph, each correct to three decimal places.

This misses the negative zero; a window starting at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> hides the crossing near <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -0.7</annotation></semantics></math>.

These are the zeros of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-x)</annotation></semantics></math>: every sign is flipped, as if the graph were reflected across the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis.

These are the inputs of the two turning points, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> changes direction, not where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use quadratic regression to model the data as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(x) = ax^2 + bx + c</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, correct to three decimal places?

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.286</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.286</annotation></semantics></math>

Store the regression in the calculator for the next questions. The negative <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> fits counts that rise and then fall.
options: Right: the coefficient of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> in the quadratic regression.

This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, the coefficient of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, not the coefficient of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, the constant term of the regression.
This is the slope of a linear regression on the same data, a different model.

options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>36.571</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.571</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.000</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9.143</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-9.143</annotation></semantics></math>

options: This is the change <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(5) - V(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, not divided by the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> weeks.

This uses the table values <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>42</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>78</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78</annotation></semantics></math>; the question asks about the model <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>.

This subtracts in the wrong order: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(1) - V(5)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 - 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: the slope of the secant line of the model on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 5]</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A town had <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}200</annotation></semantics></math> residents at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>950</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}950</annotation></semantics></math> residents at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in years. An exponential model <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(t) = ab^t</annotation></semantics></math> passes through both points. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, correct to three decimal places?
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.625</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.625</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.084</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.084</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.104</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.104</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.072</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 1{,}200</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>950</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}200b^6 = 1{,}950</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1.625</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^6 = 1.625</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1.625</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.084</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 1.625^{1/6} \approx 1.084</annotation></semantics></math>: the population grows by about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> a year.
options: This is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^6</annotation></semantics></math>, the growth factor over all six years, not over one year.

Right: the sixth root of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>950</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1{,}950}{1{,}200}</annotation></semantics></math>, the growth factor per year.

options: This is the change <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>100</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(100) - D(60)</annotation></semantics></math>, not divided by the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> days.

This subtracts in the wrong order: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>100</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(60) - D(100)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100 - 60</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: the slope of the secant line on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[60, 100]</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is the calculator in degree mode; in radians the change is much larger.

why.correct: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3\sin(2x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 1 + x</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math> in radian mode. The line crosses the first hump of the sine curve twice: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.207</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 0.207</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.167</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.167</annotation></semantics></math>. After that the sine curve is below the line.
options: This misses the second crossing, where the sine curve falls back below the line.

This is what degree mode shows; in radians the curves cross twice.
